drafts.draft_en:
$100k on a degree is "investing in yourself."

$100k into a Philly rowhome bought at 65% of after-repair value is "too risky."

Which one pays you back first?
drafts.pattern: Debt-framing fork (TheREDevGUY's student loans vs rental debt question) in the one-line question format (Cardone at 242.3k). Grounded in Bar's 65% all-in rule. No promised returns.
drafts.video_tip: Talking head, 12s. Hold up a diploma in one hand and a rowhome photo in the other. Put '65% of ARV' on screen and end on 'Which one pays you back first?'

drafts.draft_en:
A Philly rental brings in [RENT]/month.

That's [RENT x 12] a year. Now the real numbers:

[TAXES + INSURANCE]
[MORTGAGE INTEREST]
[REPAIRS RESERVE]
[VACANCY]

What's left: [NET].

That's why I buy at 65% of ARV. The buy price is the only line you control.
drafts.pattern: Line-by-line breakdown, same structure as HughInvests' 13.5k post. Placeholders on purpose: fill in real numbers from one of your own deals before posting. Don't use made-up figures.
drafts.video_tip: Screen record, 20s. Type each line into your notes app, one per beat. Circle the buy price at the end and say 'This is the only line you control.'
